mellah_page.hero_subtitle: Historic Jewish quarter lanes within El Jadida’s old-town fabric — quieter streets and layered heritage.
mellah_page.overview.title: A quarter of memory
mellah_page.overview.p1: El Jadida’s Mellah is the historic Jewish quarter woven into the wider old town. Lanes are quieter than the main souk arteries; the interest is atmosphere and urban history more than monuments.
mellah_page.overview.p2: Walk respectfully, keep photography discreet around homes, and use the Mellah as part of a broader medina loop rather than a long standalone stop.
mellah_page.overview.p3: Pair it with the Portuguese walls and the fishing port for a full reading of the town’s communities and trades.

mellah_page.faq.title: Old Jewish Mellah FAQ
mellah_page.faq.q1.question: Is there a ticket?
mellah_page.faq.q1.answer: No. It is a living neighbourhood of streets to walk.
mellah_page.faq.q2.question: Guided tours?
mellah_page.faq.q2.answer: Local guides can add context if you want names and stories.
mellah_page.faq.q3.question: How long?
mellah_page.faq.q3.answer: About an hour within a wider medina walk.
mellah_page.faq.q4.question: Safe?
mellah_page.faq.q4.answer: Daytime is usual; stick to busier connecting lanes if unsure.
mellah_page.faq.q5.question: Combine with souks?
mellah_page.faq.q5.answer: Yes — the Mellah and market streets sit in the same old-town fabric.
